2
What is the vertical component of this displacement vector?
5.0 km
37°
horizontal
A
3.0 km
B
3.8 km
C
4.0 km
D
5.0 km

hints: Look at the diagram: the $5.0 \text{ km}$ arrow makes $37^{\circ}$ with the horizontal dashed line, so the vertical side is opposite that angle.
Connect opposite and hypotenuse with sine: vertical component $= 5.0 \text{ km} \times \sin 37^{\circ}$ for an angle measured from the horizontal.
Evaluate $5.0 \times \sin 37^{\circ}$ and compare with $5.0 \times \cos 37^{\circ}$ to check which one is the shorter vertical side.
walkthrough: Identify the given data from the diagram: hypotenuse magnitude $= 5.0 \text{ km}$ and angle to the horizontal $= 37^{\circ}$.
State the resolution rule: when the angle is measured from the horizontal, vertical component $= R \sin \theta$ and horizontal component $= R \cos \theta$.
Set up the vertical calculation: $R_v = 5.0 \text{ km} \times \sin 37^{\circ}$.
Substitute $\sin 37^{\circ} \approx 0.60$: $R_v \approx 5.0 \times 0.60 = 3.0 \text{ km}$ with unit $\text{km}$ as for displacement.
Note the horizontal component would be $5.0 \cos 37^{\circ} \approx 4.0 \text{ km}$, confirming the vertical side is the shorter $3.0 \text{ km}$ side.
Match $3.0 \text{ km}$ to the options. This is option A.

A.explanation: Vertical component is $5.0 \sin 37^{\circ} \approx 3.0 \text{ km}$, opposite the $37^{\circ}$ angle to the horizontal.

B.explanation: 3.8 km is close to $5.0 \cos 37^{\circ}$, which is the horizontal adjacent component, not the vertical component.

C.explanation: 4.0 km is $5.0 \cos 37^{\circ}$, the component along the horizontal dashed line, not the vertical component.

D.explanation: 5.0 km is the magnitude of the full displacement vector, not its resolved vertical part.
